title: decision: duplicate question rewritten into a new question

items.flag: duplicate of intermediate module m06-the-professional-reading 3 (near p0.72 k0.62): both ask what reading the 0.850000 likelihood as a posterior does, key 298.2500 against 207.7989
items.reason: True duplicate across tiers, also asked in advanced final 25; kept the intermediate m06 question and rewrote this copy to test the m06 onward point on capital portfolio decisions.

prompt.old: An expert reads the EKPAN lottery survey's likelihood of 0.850000, a bright spot given success, as the chance of success after a bright spot. What does that do to the drill after a bright spot?
prompt.new: The onward lesson takes decision analysis on to capital portfolio decisions under one budget. Why is the best set of projects not simply the set of individually best ones?

explanation.old: Bayes turns 0.850000 into 0.646739 because a bright spot also appears on 0.250000 of dry holes, which makes a bright spot 0.460000 likely overall. 9.2361 is the farm-out's value after no bright spot.
explanation.new: Capital portfolio decisions choose among many projects under one budget, and money spent on one is unavailable to the next, so the choice is of a set under that constraint. Decision Studio already sets capital allocation from a saved portfolio beside the decision analysis in one brief.

0.old: Nothing to the value, because a likelihood and a posterior are the same number whenever the survey passes its consistency check.
0.new: Because each project's EMV has to be turned into a net value of information before projects on different prospects can be compared at all.

1.old: It values the drill at 207.7989 regardless, because the engine converts any typed 0.850000 into the posterior before weighting the drill.
1.new: Because a portfolio rolls every project back at the discount rate of its riskiest member, which lowers each value unevenly and so reorders them.

2.old: It values the drill at 298.2500 in place of 207.7989, because the posterior after a bright spot is 0.646739.
2.new: Because money spent on one project is unavailable to the next, so each is judged against what else the same budget buys.

3.old: It lowers the drill after a bright spot to 9.2361, since that likelihood belongs to the reading on which the farm-out is chosen.
3.new: Because an individually best project was valued with its own information already bought, and a portfolio has to strip every survey value out first.

items.correct_change_reason: True duplicate rewritten into a new question on a different point, so the key is new text for the new question.
